title: Introduce operator-proof-aggregator and geo-zone KMS router
author: Asha Raman
description:
Motivation: operator-facing requests (operator impersonation, session-bound escalations) require stronger non-repudiation and region-aware keying for compliance. This PR introduces two cooperating pieces: (1) operator-proof-aggregator, a small service that validates operator PoP claims (session JWTs), canonicalizes operator metadata and emits a signed proof envelope; and (2) geozone-kms-router, a routing shim that maps a proof envelope + service region to a jurisdiction-appropriate KMS key and forwards signing/wrapping requests while annotating audit headers. Together they reduce cross-region key misuse, provide clearer audit proofs and enable RBAC v2 policies to reason over operator-originated actions.

What changed (high level): added a new service package under services/operator-proof-aggregator, a lightweight router under internal/kms/router, RBAC v2 policy templates for operator-bound actions, and audit plumbing to attach proof hashes to existing audit-aggregator pipeline. The implementation is intentionally conservative: proofs are HMAC-signed locally then wrapped with region-bound CMKs before being emitted to the audit queue. This keeps the fast-path single-round-trip while ensuring the audit envelope is verifiable and residency-aware.

Small illustrative snippet (envelope canonicalization):
- canonicalize operator claims -> stable JSON ordering -> sha256 -> hmac(local_key)
This is intentionally terse; the full builder is in envelope.go and includes versioning to support future migration.

Rollout plan: feature flagged behind feature.operator_proof_aggregator. Staged rollout in three phases: (1) internal-only (dev + staging) for 2 days; (2) internal + trusted customers (beta) for 7 days; (3) broad rollout with RBAC template migration (automated dry-run first). During rollout the router uses soft-fail semantics: if region-specific CMK unavailable, it falls back to configured multi-region wrapping with an explicit audit tag.

Backward-compatibility: audit consumers that don't parse X-Redwood-Proof-Hash will continue to function; new UI surface (audit proof details) is optional. RBAC migration is additive: templates include an opt-in flag and migration script annotates operator roles with operator:bound=true.

Testing performed: unit tests (envelope builder, validator), integration (e2e test simulating KMS failover and audit ingestion), load test (1000 ops/s canonicalization in CI run, 95th percentile extra latency +4ms), and manual inspection of audit artifacts for two sample tenants.

Related work/PRs: references to SEC-78 (policy proofing), and a follow-up PR will introduce a policy-linter rule that flags operator-bound RBAC rules lacking proof requirements.

Notes on security posture: proofs are timestamped and have a short TTL (default 10s). The aggregator does not persist raw operator secrets; only canonicalized claims and a truncated proof-hash are emitted. The region router enforces CMK usage via account-scoped policy and adds an immutable audit header documenting the key id (redwood-kms://eu-west-1/alias/operator-proofs).

Migration steps for operators: run the migration script in a dry-run, opt-in roles to operator:bound, enable feature flag, verify audit UI for expected proof entries, then flip full rollout.
